title: Bonus Episode: Coronavirus Anxiety (Part 2) with Baruch Fischhoff, PhD

sentences.en: Welcome to this special bonus episode of Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听美国心理学会旗舰播客《心理学谈话》的这期特别加更节目。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology explores the connections between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》旨在探索心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Turn on the evening news or open a newspaper these days, and there's virtually nothing but COVID-19 coverage.
sentences.zh: 如今，只要打开晚间新闻或翻开报纸，几乎全是关于新冠肺炎的报道。

sentences.en: The story is moving as rapidly as the coronavirus itself.
sentences.zh: 疫情的发展速度正如病毒本身一样迅猛。

sentences.en: Here on Speaking of Psychology, we acted quickly to offer a psychological perspective on the novel coronavirus,
sentences.zh: 在《心理学谈话》节目中，我们迅速采取行动，从心理学角度解读这种新型冠状病毒，

sentences.en: doing our first interview on the topic on February 10th, which now seems like a lifetime ago.
sentences.zh: 并于2月10日就该话题进行了首次采访，那感觉仿佛已是上辈子的事了。

sentences.en: Back then, the coronavirus had barely touched U.S.
sentences.zh: 当时，新冠病毒几乎还没有触及美国，

sentences.en: shores.
sentences.zh: 海岸线。

sentences.en: Life was mundane.
sentences.zh: 生活还很平淡。

sentences.en: Schools were open.
sentences.zh: 学校照常开放。

sentences.en: Most of us had jobs or weren't teleworking.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都有工作，或者不需要远程办公。

sentences.en: And our understanding of the nature of the coronavirus was limited.
sentences.zh: 而且我们对这种冠状病毒本质的了解还很有限。

sentences.en: Indeed, it is still limited, but we do know more now.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在依然有限，但我们确实比那时知道得更多了。

sentences.en: And the United States has the dubious distinction as being the country with the most coronavirus infections today.
sentences.zh: 而且美国如今不幸成为了新冠感染病例最多的国家。

sentences.en: On February 10th, we aired an interview with Dr. Baruch Fischhoff, a professor at the Institute for Politics and Strategy
sentences.zh: 在2月10日，我们播出了对巴鲁克·费施霍夫博士的采访，他是卡内基梅隆大学政治与战略研究所

sentences.en: and the Department of Engineering and Public Policy at Carnegie Mellon University.
sentences.zh: 以及工程与公共政策系的教授。

sentences.en: He's also an expert on public perception of risk and human judgment and decision making.
sentences.zh: 他也是公众风险感知、人类判断与决策方面的专家。

sentences.en: He provided some important insights into quarantine and the risk of the virus, along with helpful advice on how to deal with anxiety.
sentences.zh: 他为隔离和病毒风险提供了一些重要的见解，并就如何应对焦虑给出了有益的建议。

sentences.en: But since much has changed in the ensuing month and a half, we have invited Dr. Fischhoff back to talk about the latest developments regarding the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但由于过去一个半月里发生了很大变化，我们再次邀请费施霍夫博士来谈谈疫情的最新进展。

sentences.en: So welcome back to Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Fischhoff.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《心理学谈话》，费施霍夫博士。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you for having me back.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你们再次邀请我。

sentences.en: And you're right, February 10th does seem like a lifetime ago.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，2月10日确实感觉像是上辈子的事了。

sentences.en: It really does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So as I said a moment ago, we know more about the coronavirus today than we did when you last spoke to APA.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才所说，今天我们对新冠病毒的了解比你上次接受美国心理学会采访时要多。

sentences.en: So given that, would you say the risk level, at least in the United States, has changed since then?
sentences.zh: 那么鉴于此，你会说风险水平，至少在美国，从那时起发生了变化吗？

sentences.en: Or is it the same as it has always been, but now we have more information and better understand the risk?
sentences.zh: 还是说风险一直没变，只是现在我们掌握了更多信息，对风险有了更好的理解？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's some of both.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为两者皆有。

sentences.en: I think the head, the country responded in a more coordinated and an energetic way, then we would be facing less risk than we have now.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果国家能以更协调、更有力的方式做出反应，我们现在面临的风险就会小一些。

sentences.en: We didn't really mobilize for much of that time.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，我们并没有真正动员起来。

sentences.en: We had a major heads up from what was going on with China.
sentences.zh: 我们从中国发生的情况中得到了重要的预警。

sentences.en: Many, I would say, science-oriented organizations like my university and others, some of the big tech firms, began planning in January.
sentences.zh: 许多科学导向的组织，比如我的大学和其他机构，以及一些大型科技公司，在1月份就开始了规划。

sentences.en: But the United States was very sluggish, didn't get into gear.
sentences.zh: 但美国行动非常迟缓，没有进入状态。

sentences.en: So we're facing a bigger risk now than we needed to have been facing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在面临的风险比本应面临的要大。

sentences.en: So you spoke the last time about people being more fearful of things that they don't know compared with things they do know.
sentences.zh: 你上次提到，相比于已知的事物，人们对未知的事物会感到更加恐惧。

sentences.en: And this was in the context of how we have a good understanding of how much threat is posed by seasonal flu.
sentences.zh: 这是在我们对季节性流感造成的威胁有充分了解的背景下讨论的。

sentences.en: But we now know more about the coronavirus, including that it's more easily transmitted by flu and that it seems to be more lethal.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在对新冠病毒了解更多了，包括它比流感更容易传播，而且似乎更致命。

sentences.en: So given that we know more, should we be less fearful of COVID-19 or should we be more fearful right now?
sentences.zh: 既然我们了解得更多了，我们现在应该减少对新冠肺炎的恐惧，还是应该更加恐惧？

sentences.en: Well, we should be properly fearful that each of us needs to consider what are the risks to themselves and to other people associated with each of their actions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们应该保持适当的恐惧，每个人都需要考虑自己的每一个行为会给自己和他人带来什么风险。

sentences.en: So when we expose ourselves, then we not only take on risks for ourselves, but we, you know, should worse comes to worse.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们让自己暴露在风险中时，我们不仅是在承担自己的风险，而且，你知道，如果情况变得更糟，

sentences.en: And we need hospitalization.
sentences.zh: 我们需要住院治疗，

sentences.en: We're imposing risks on the health care system.
sentences.zh: 我们就是在给医疗系统增加负担。

sentences.en: If we have a suspicion of having been exposed and we're required to isolate, then we're imposing a burden on other people.
sentences.zh: 如果我们怀疑自己曾暴露在病毒中并被要求隔离，那么我们就是在给他人增加负担。

sentences.en: And if we actually have the disease and, you know, perhaps are fortunate enough to have a asymptomatic or light, light case,
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的患了病，你知道，也许幸运地是无症状或轻症，

sentences.en: we become disease vectors and are capable of transmitting it to every to everybody.
sentences.zh: 我们就会成为疾病传播者，有能力把它传染给每一个人。

sentences.en: So this is for our own sake and for other people's sake.
sentences.zh: 所以这既是为了我们自己，也是为了他人。

sentences.en: This is a life and death situation.
sentences.zh: 这是一场关乎生死的局面。

sentences.en: And we should take it with the gravity that it deserves.
sentences.zh: 我们应该以它应有的严肃态度来对待。

sentences.en: That also means not overstating it.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着不要夸大其词。

sentences.en: That is, that is, we need to find, each of us needs to find a balance where we're doing all that we appropriately, appropriately can.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们需要找到平衡，每个人都需要在力所能及的范围内尽一切努力。

sentences.en: And then, and then kind of give ourselves a break and not worry about it, you know, in ways that we can no longer control.
sentences.zh: 然后，让自己放松一下，不要再为那些我们无法控制的事情而担忧。

sentences.en: So, how can we tell what risks we're taking when we do certain things?
sentences.zh: 那么，当我们做某些事情时，我们如何判断自己正在承担什么样的风险？

sentences.en: So, I mean, all of us have to eat.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们所有人都得吃饭。

sentences.en: Is it a problem to go to the grocery store?
sentences.zh: 去杂货店是个问题吗？

sentences.en: What about going out and running, taking a run or a walk or a ride on a bike?
sentences.zh: 出去跑步、散步或骑自行车怎么样？

sentences.en: What about taking in our packages from Amazon?
sentences.zh: 接收亚马逊的包裹怎么样？

sentences.en: I mean, what sorts of things are more or less dangerous?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，哪些事情危险程度更高或更低？

sentences.en: Well, I'm not a toxicologist or a public health official.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不是毒理学家或公共卫生官员。

sentences.en: So, I would recommend to people to find a very small number of very trustworthy sources, perhaps their local health department.
sentences.zh: 所以我建议人们寻找极少数非常值得信赖的来源，比如当地的卫生部门。

sentences.en: They're also often a very good source and they're not subject to the politics,
sentences.zh: 他们通常也是非常好的信息来源，而且不受政治因素的影响，

sentences.en: political pressures that say the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention or the World Health Organization experience.
sentences.zh: 不受像美国疾病控制与预防中心或世界卫生组织所面临的那种政治压力。

sentences.en: Or find a science writer who's been working this beat, knows how to evaluate scientific evidence and find the guidance that they have.
sentences.zh: 或者找一位长期关注该领域的科学记者，他们知道如何评估科学证据，并从中获取指导。

sentences.en: I think the science is actually advancing fairly quickly on understanding the persistence of the virus in the air and on different package surfaces.
sentences.zh: 我认为在理解病毒在空气中和不同包装表面的持久性方面，科学实际上正在迅速进步。

sentences.en: So, I would say, you know, it may be different now, science may be different two weeks from now than it is now.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，你知道，现在的情况可能与两周后不同，科学结论可能也会有所改变。

sentences.en: So, rather than giving anything specific, I suggest that people find some of those sources.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其给出具体的建议，我建议人们去寻找那些权威来源。

sentences.en: One thing that complicates this for all of us is that because our national response has been and remains so feeble in many ways,
sentences.zh: 有一件事让所有人都感到困惑，那就是由于我们的国家应对措施在许多方面一直很软弱，

sentences.en: we are not doing the kind of testing that would give us a clear idea of how much of the disease is out there.
sentences.zh: 我们没有进行那种能让我们清楚了解疫情规模的检测。

sentences.en: And it would be different if we knew for certain that one person in our area was seropositive or had the disease.
sentences.zh: 如果我们确定我们所在地区有一个人血清呈阳性或患有该病，情况就会不同。

sentences.en: Or if we thought that one person in 10 had it, it would be very different in terms of thinking about how one would navigate it.
sentences.zh: 或者如果我们认为每10个人里有一个人感染，那么在考虑如何应对时，情况也会大不相同。

sentences.en: So, we don't know exactly what the risk is, but it's probably, I don't know where I'm writing, talking from Pittsburgh.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不知道确切的风险是多少，但我不知道，我正在匹兹堡跟你通话，

sentences.en: I wouldn't be surprised if it's 2% to 5% of people have some reasonable chance of having been exposed to the disease.
sentences.zh: 如果说有2%到5%的人有相当大的可能性接触过这种疾病，我一点也不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And again, because the testing is so poor, we have very little idea where those people are.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，因为检测太糟糕了，我们几乎不知道这些人都在哪里。

sentences.en: So, we might as well assume that whatever the rate is, it's equally likely to be anybody, which suggests that, well,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不妨假设无论感染率是多少，任何人都同样可能被感染，这意味着，嗯，

sentences.en: if a 2% chance of getting the disease from somebody is more than you want to deal with,
sentences.zh: 如果从某人那里感染疾病的2%的风险是你不想面对的，

sentences.en: then it would be important to maintain the kind of social distancing that's being recommended.
sentences.zh: 那么保持所建议的那种社交距离就很重要了。

sentences.en: So, I've seen some videos on the internet of people who claim to be doctors unpacking groceries and showing how you should wash off everything.
sentences.zh: 我曾在网上看到一些自称是医生的视频，他们拆开杂货，展示你应该如何清洗所有东西。

sentences.en: I mean, to a level that seems absolutely crazy to me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种程度对我来说简直是疯了。

sentences.en: I mean, is that really the risk that we're facing right now?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的是我们现在面临的风险吗？

sentences.en: Do these people know what they're talking about?
sentences.zh: 这些人知道他们在说什么吗？

sentences.en: And where should we be getting this kind of information?
sentences.zh: 我们应该从哪里获取这类信息？

sentences.en: So, I would say once again, I think it's, again, part of our national failure to plan for and respond to this disease.
sentences.zh: 所以，我还是要说，我认为这再次反映了我们国家在规划和应对这种疾病方面的失败。

sentences.en: That really, somebody ought to have taken the best available evidence and translate it into the practical terms that everybody needs to know.
sentences.zh: 真的，应该有人把现有的最佳证据转化为每个人都需要知道的实用术语。

sentences.en: Because everybody eats, everybody handles groceries, and because we don't have national guidance, that people are left looking for somebody somewhere.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都要吃饭，每个人都要处理杂货，而且因为我们没有国家层面的指导，人们只能到处寻找信息。

sentences.en: So, in my experience, the internet is a, the wild internet is, untamed internet is not a very good source of information.
sentences.zh: 所以，根据我的经验，互联网，那个狂野、不受约束的互联网，并不是一个很好的信息来源。

sentences.en: So, once again, I would look for science reporters who know how to evaluate evidence, and they may very well have covered it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我还是会寻找那些懂得如何评估证据的科学记者，他们很可能已经报道过这些内容了。

sentences.en: Somebody that you, you know, somebody that you trust, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 找一个你信任的人，我不知道，

sentences.en: Scientific American or Wired or Undark or the science or health reporters from one of the major newspapers that still have them.
sentences.zh: 比如《科学美国人》、《连线》杂志、《Undark》或者那些依然保留科学或健康版块的主流报纸的记者。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the confusing things that's happened in this situation is we now have political beat reporters covering topics in health.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种情况中令人困惑的一点是，我们现在有政治记者在报道健康话题。

sentences.en: And they're, you know, they may have expertise in evaluating politicians' claims, but they don't have expertise in evaluating scientific evidence.
sentences.zh: 他们可能擅长评估政客的言论，但他们并不擅长评估科学证据。

sentences.en: Well, then there's the problem of those reporters who are out there, let's say, covering the president's daily briefings on this situation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有那些在现场报道总统每日疫情简报的记者的问题。

sentences.en: And you never know from day to day what he's going to say, he gets up there, and it's not so much to single him out, but it's kind of inescapable.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道他明天会说什么，他站到台上，这倒不是要特意针对他，但这确实是无法回避的。

sentences.en: He'll say something on Monday and on Tuesday, he'll correct himself, and on Wednesday, Dr. Anthony Fauci will say something else.
sentences.zh: 他周一说了一些话，周二又纠正自己，周三安东尼·福奇博士又会说些别的。

sentences.en: I mean, what are reasonable people to think when we're being bombarded with this kind of, I mean, we're whipsawed by the stats that we're given and the information that we're told.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我们被这些信息轰炸时，我们被给出的数据和被告知的信息搞得晕头转向，理智的人该怎么想？

sentences.en: Yeah, so whatever the source, inconsistent, conflicting evidence adds to the burden that we're all bearing in this crisis.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以无论来源如何，不一致、相互矛盾的证据只会增加我们在这次危机中承受的负担。

sentences.en: The standard recommendation in this situation and others is look to subject matter experts or, again,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，标准的建议是寻找主题专家，或者再次强调，

sentences.en: experienced science or health reporters for evidence and pay no attention to science or health information that comes from politicians.
sentences.zh: 寻找经验丰富的科学或健康记者获取证据，不要理会政客提供的科学或健康信息。

sentences.en: That even if they, in good faith, are trying to tell you the truth and not spin it for political advantage, they don't know how to evaluate scientific claiMs.
sentences.zh: 即使他们是出于好意试图告诉你真相，而不是为了政治利益进行粉饰，他们也不知道如何评估科学主张。

sentences.en: Even if they've been briefed, they don't have the mental models, the training, the background to communicate anything.
sentences.zh: 即使他们听取了简报，他们也没有沟通这些信息所需的思维模型、训练和背景。

sentences.en: So it's look at political figures to understand where they are in the political arena, whether or not you trust them.
sentences.zh: 所以，关注政治人物是为了了解他们在政治舞台上的立场，无论你是否信任他们。

sentences.en: If they inspire you, then take in their inspirational messages.
sentences.zh: 如果他们激励了你，那就接受他们的激励信息。

sentences.en: But they're no more a source of information than the sort of stuff that shows up in social media.
sentences.zh: 但他们提供的信息来源并不比社交媒体上出现的东西更可靠。

sentences.en: So health people and scientists for health and science information, politicians for politics.
sentences.zh: 所以，健康和科学信息要找健康专家和科学家，政治问题才找政客。

sentences.en: There's a lot of talk out there about exponential growth of the coronavirus infections.
sentences.zh: 外界有很多关于新冠病毒感染呈指数级增长的讨论。

sentences.en: What exactly does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: You've studied flu, for example.
sentences.zh: 你研究过流感，例如。

sentences.en: Does the flu grow exponentially?
sentences.zh: 流感会呈指数级增长吗？

sentences.en: Is this something that we see on a regular basis with other kinds of illnesses?
sentences.zh: 这是我们在其他疾病中经常看到的情况吗？

sentences.en: So any transmissible disease has what they call a reproduction factor.
sentences.zh: 任何传染性疾病都有所谓的繁殖系数。

sentences.en: And the technical term is R-naught.
sentences.zh: 技术术语是R0（基本传染数）。

sentences.en: And it's basically for each person who gets the disease, how many people get the disease from them.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是每个感染者会把疾病传染给多少人。

sentences.en: So measles has an R-naught, the reproduction factor in the teens.
sentences.zh: 麻疹的R0值在十几左右。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, for those who've had any experience with it, it just spreads like wildfire, which means that it spreads like wildfire.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些有相关经验的人来说，它传播起来就像野火一样，这意味着它传播得极快。

sentences.en: So it seems as though at the time we're writing as though the reproduction factor for the current virus is maybe two or three.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们录制节目时，这种病毒的繁殖系数似乎在二到三之间。

sentences.en: So that means that for each person who gets it, say another two people get it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着每个感染者会传染给另外两个人。

sentences.en: But then each of those gives it to another people and each of those gives it to two additional people.
sentences.zh: 然后这两个人中的每一个人又会传染给另外两个人，以此类推。

sentences.en: So eventually it raises to the – it's two to some exponent by the time you cascade it.
sentences.zh: 所以最终它会上升到——当你级联计算时，它是二的某个指数次方。

sentences.en: That's why it's so important in places like South Korea where they have done – or Singapore where they've done an effective job or a much more effective job than we have at containing the disease is they do a lot of testing.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在韩国或新加坡这样做得有效，或者比我们做得有效得多的地方，他们进行了大量的检测，从而控制住了疾病。

sentences.en: They find that first person as quickly as they can.
sentences.zh: 他们会尽快找到第一个感染者。

sentences.en: They trace everybody who they might have exposed and who might subsequently expose other people so that you stop that cascade.
sentences.zh: 他们追踪所有可能被感染的人，以及那些随后可能感染他人的人，从而阻止这种级联传播。

sentences.en: You can only do that if you do a lot of testing and have really mobilized your resources.
sentences.zh: 只有进行大量检测并真正调动资源，你才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: One of the – from an intuitive perspective though, it's hard to see how those probabilities,
sentences.zh: 不过从直觉角度来看，很难看出那些概率，

sentences.en: either how that exponential process that two and then four and then eight and 16 mounts up.
sentences.zh: 无论是那种二、四、八、十六的指数增长过程是如何累积的。

sentences.en: And it's a situation where even if you have a degree in math like I do, know how to do the calculations, your intuitions will lead you wrong.
sentences.zh: 即使你有像我这样的数学学位，知道如何进行计算，你的直觉也会把你带入歧途。

sentences.en: So you really have to look at the numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的必须看数据。

sentences.en: If somebody says this is where it's going and they've done a trustworthy peer-reviewed analysis, then believe their numbers, not your intuition.
sentences.zh: 如果有人说这就是发展趋势，并且他们做了值得信赖的同行评审分析，那么请相信他们的数据，而不是你的直觉。

sentences.en: So there are different models out there right now though.
sentences.zh: 不过现在确实有不同的模型。

sentences.en: I mean how do we know which ones to believe in?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们怎么知道该相信哪一个？

sentences.en: And some of them do seem to be coming from reputable sources.
sentences.zh: 而且其中一些似乎确实来自可靠的来源。

sentences.en: So the models, what they do, they do things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以模型，它们所做的，就是做类似的事情。

sentences.en: They say, well, what's the probability that – they put together pieces and then do the math for you.
sentences.zh: 它们会说，好吧，概率是多少——它们把各个部分拼凑在一起，然后为你进行数学计算。

sentences.en: So they say, how many people have it?
sentences.zh: 所以它们会说，有多少人感染了？

sentences.en: How many people will they give it to?
sentences.zh: 他们会传染给多少人？

sentences.en: What percentage of those people will need hospitalization?
sentences.zh: 这些人中有多少比例需要住院治疗？

sentences.en: What's our ability to reduce that transmission rate by social distancing?
sentences.zh: 我们通过社交距离减少传播率的能力如何？

sentences.en: And they just do – they do the math for you and you could never do that in your head.
sentences.zh: 它们只是为你做了数学计算，而你在脑子里是永远算不出来的。

sentences.en: But the quality of the model depends on how complete they are and how good these pieces are.
sentences.zh: 但模型的质量取决于它们有多完整，以及这些组成部分有多好。

sentences.en: So at this point, again, because we've done such a poor job of testing, we're sort of fuzzy about – we're in a fuzzy, uncertain state about the transmission rate of the disease.
sentences.zh: 所以目前，还是因为我们的检测工作做得太差，我们对疾病的传播率处于一种模糊、不确定的状态。

sentences.en: And there's also rather little social science in the – you could think of this as – well, social distancing, that's really a psychological or a sociological question.
sentences.zh: 而且社会科学在其中的应用也相当少——你可以把它看作——嗯，社交距离，这实际上是一个心理学或社会学问题。

sentences.en: That is, how well do people understand what social distancing is?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，人们对社交距离的理解程度如何？

sentences.en: How well are they able to manage it in their everyday affairs?
sentences.zh: 他们在日常事务中管理社交距离的能力如何？

sentences.en: Affairs, when you're having a conversation with somebody who starts – you start off six feet apart and it's a conversation and you want to talk to one,
sentences.zh: 当你和某人交谈时，你们开始时保持六英尺的距离，这只是一次谈话，你想和某人交谈，

sentences.en: will you be drifting together?
sentences.zh: 你们会不自觉地靠近吗？

sentences.en: So how well social distancing works is really a behavioral question and there's – they're very – typically these models don't have – the modeler – modeling teams typically don't have a lot of social science expertise.
sentences.zh: 所以社交距离的效果如何，实际上是一个行为问题，而且通常这些模型——建模团队通常没有太多的社会科学专业知识。

sentences.en: It turns out that the social sciences is, as they say, unsettled.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，社会科学正如人们所说，是不确定的。

sentences.en: But as we really don't know how effective these things are partly because we haven't studied them as well as we want.
sentences.zh: 但由于我们确实不知道这些措施有多有效，部分原因是我们没有像我们希望的那样深入研究它们。

sentences.en: If your listeners are interested, our listeners are interested,
sentences.zh: 如果你的听众感兴趣，我们的听众感兴趣的话，

sentences.en: the National Academy of Sciences has a consensus committee that reports to the Office of Science and Technology Policy in the White House that I've just been asked to join that has done a report on –
sentences.zh: 美国国家科学院有一个共识委员会，向白宫科技政策办公室报告，我刚被邀请加入，他们做了一份关于——

sentences.en: a synthetic report on social – effectiveness of social distancing.
sentences.zh: 一份关于社交距离有效性的综合报告。

sentences.en: It's pretty technical, but it's also pretty readable.
sentences.zh: 它相当专业，但也相当易读。

sentences.en: But that committee has been turning out reports on things, some of them quite short, like they have a two-page report on how long the virus persists on different surfaces.
sentences.zh: 但该委员会一直在发布关于各种事物的报告，其中一些非常简短，比如他们有一份两页的报告，关于病毒在不同表面上能存活多久。

sentences.en: So if you wanted to know how to bring in the groceries, that would be a place where you could figure it out yourself or hope that a science writer had done it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想知道如何去采购杂货，那你可以自己摸索，或者寄希望于有科普作家写过相关内容。

sentences.en: This committee just turned out a report on really sort of preparing for worse.
sentences.zh: 这个委员会刚刚发布了一份关于如何应对更糟糕情况的报告。

sentences.en: It's on what they call critical care standards.
sentences.zh: 报告的主题是他们所谓的重症监护标准。

sentences.en: So they pull together a consensus of what the – I guess the healthcare or medical,
sentences.zh: 他们汇集了各方共识，关于——我想应该是医疗或医学界，

sentences.en: bioethical establishment believes that should be done in situations where we don't have enough equipment or perhaps enough healthcare personnel to be able to treat – give everybody the usual standard of care.
sentences.zh: 生物伦理学界认为，在设备不足或医护人员不足，无法为所有人提供常规护理标准的情况下，应该采取什么措施。

sentences.en: So it's basically guidance on rationing healthcare in a situation where we haven't mustered the resources in order to give everybody a reasonable standard of care.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是在资源不足以让每个人都获得合理护理标准的情况下，关于如何分配医疗资源的指导意见。

sentences.en: It's kind of – it's a grim document, but if somebody would like to read a summary of thinking, you can find it there.
sentences.zh: 这份文件读起来有些沉重，但如果有人想阅读相关思路的总结，可以在那里找到。

sentences.en: Sorry, say again where it's findable?
sentences.zh: 抱歉，能再说一遍在哪里可以找到吗？

sentences.en: It's called the National Academy of Sciences Standing Committee on – if people go to the national – nas.edu, the nationalacademyofsciences.edu,
sentences.zh: 它是由美国国家科学院常设委员会发布的——如果人们访问国家科学院的网站 nas.edu，即 nationalacademyofsciences.edu，

sentences.en: look at their – they feature COVID-19 news and resources.
sentences.zh: 查看他们的页面——他们有关于新冠肺炎的新闻和资源专栏。

sentences.en: If you click there, you can find this committee.
sentences.zh: 点击那里，你就能找到这个委员会。

sentences.en: It's got a long URL itself.
sentences.zh: 它本身的网址很长。

sentences.en: And I think it is addressing a problem that you mentioned earlier, which is, oh, there's lots of people giving advice.
sentences.zh: 我认为它解决了一个你之前提到的问题，那就是，哦，有太多人在提供建议了。

sentences.en: How do we know who to trust?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何知道该信任谁？

sentences.en: So the National Academy, at the request of the federal government, has taken it upon themselves to produce peer-reviewed syntheses of what the evidence says at any given time.
sentences.zh: 因此，美国国家科学院应联邦政府的要求，承担起了对现有证据进行同行评审并汇总的责任。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: That would be interesting to look at.
sentences.zh: 那值得一看。

sentences.en: So talking about social distancing, and I don't know that we have a lot of research in this area, but perhaps you would know – I mean,
sentences.zh: 谈到社交距离，我不确定我们在这个领域是否有大量研究，但也许你了解——我的意思是，

sentences.en: we've studied – psychology has certainly studied social isolation, people who have lived in solitary confinement for periods of time, and we know how they react to that.
sentences.zh: 我们研究过——心理学界确实研究过社会隔离，研究过那些长期处于单独监禁中的人，我们知道他们对此有何反应。

sentences.en: Do we have any idea about social distancing and how long people will tolerate it?
sentences.zh: 我们对社交距离以及人们能忍受多久有概念吗？

sentences.en: I mean, are we going to reach a point in a month from now where people say, the hell with it, I can't stand this anymore, I've got to have a party?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一个月后我们是否会达到一个临界点，人们会说，去他的，我受不了了，我必须开个派对？

sentences.en: Well, that's – I would say that's at the fringes of my expertise.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这——我想这超出了我的专业范围。

sentences.en: I would say – looking at it from a decision-making perspective, one of the burdens of this period is that much of our life is no longer on automatic.
sentences.zh: 我想说——从决策的角度来看，这段时期的负担之一在于，我们生活中的许多事情不再是自动化的了。

sentences.en: That is, we get through life because we've figured out what – we've made the decisions about what we want to do, how we organize our breakfast, how we get our kids to school,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们之所以能过好生活，是因为我们已经想好了——我们已经决定了自己想做什么，如何安排早餐，如何送孩子上学，

sentences.en: when we get to work, what email we answer, and so on.
sentences.zh: 什么时候去上班，回复什么邮件，等等。

sentences.en: And if you have to make decisions about everything, it's a real burden.
sentences.zh: 如果你必须对每一件事都做出决定，那真的是一种负担。

sentences.en: And we're now in a period where all of a sudden things are up for grabs and we've got to figure them out.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正处于一个所有事情突然都变得不确定，必须重新摸索的时期。

sentences.en: And that's contributing to the burden that people feel now.
sentences.zh: 这加剧了人们现在的压力感。

sentences.en: An optimistic perspective would be that we'll – we're two weeks into this now, depending on where you are, that people will be figuring these things out,
sentences.zh: 乐观一点看，我们已经经历了两个星期——取决于你身处何地——人们会逐渐摸索出应对之道，

sentences.en: that people are using social media and more traditional ways of contacting people to develop solutions that work for them.
sentences.zh: 人们正在利用社交媒体和更传统的方式联系他人，以制定适合自己的解决方案。

sentences.en: You know, people have different ideas and different things are becoming socially norMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们有不同的想法，不同的事物正在成为社会规范。

sentences.en: So it does – it feels less aberrant now than it did three weeks ago to talk to a loved one by – on the computer, you know, on the smartphone rather than in person.
sentences.zh: 所以现在通过电脑——你知道，通过智能手机而不是面对面与亲人交谈，感觉不再像三周前那样反常了。

sentences.en: So an optimistic perspective would be – by helping one another, we'll figure out ways of dealing with this situation that work for one another and for each of us.
sentences.zh: 所以乐观地看——通过互相帮助，我们会找到适合彼此和我们每个人的应对方式。

sentences.en: And both the decision-making burden and the burden of not having a habit will lessen.
sentences.zh: 决策负担和缺乏习惯带来的负担都会减轻。

sentences.en: And then maybe our tolerance will be greater.
sentences.zh: 也许我们的忍耐力也会增强。

sentences.en: So as you said, we're a couple of weeks into this now.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我们已经经历了几个星期。

sentences.en: What are you thinking about in terms of your future research?
sentences.zh: 你对未来的研究有什么想法？

sentences.en: I mean, are you thinking that you're going to be working on reaction to coronavirus?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是否打算研究人们对新冠病毒的反应？

sentences.en: How will this figure into what you do?
sentences.zh: 这会如何融入你的工作？

sentences.en: Well, personally, I've done research on many different risks, including pandemics in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就个人而言，我过去研究过许多不同的风险，包括流行病。

sentences.en: We did a nice project – oh, I thought it was a nice project.
sentences.zh: 我们曾做过一个不错的项目——哦，我觉得那是个不错的项目。

sentences.en: We did a project on H5N1, avian flu,
sentences.zh: 我们做了一个关于H5N1禽流感的项目，

sentences.en: where we essentially mapped out what the social side of the response should be and looked at the degree of agreement between experts and non-experts.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上规划了应对措施的社会层面，并观察了专家与非专家之间的一致程度。

sentences.en: We did a study towards the end of Ebola where we looked at a national sample of Americans, courtesy of funding for the National Science Foundation,
sentences.zh: 在埃博拉疫情接近尾声时，我们做了一项研究，在国家科学基金会的资助下，我们对美国全国样本进行了调查，

sentences.en: and found that by two or three months into Ebola, people pretty well understood what was going on.
sentences.zh: 发现埃博拉疫情爆发两三个月后，人们已经相当了解情况了。

sentences.en: Even though Ebola was – there was some clumsiness in its handling together, people were able to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 尽管埃博拉疫情的处理过程中存在一些笨拙之处，但人们还是能够弄清楚情况。

sentences.en: I think that was partly because there was coordinated national policy and communication that addressed some of the noise that we're currently having, and we had good communicators.
sentences.zh: 我认为这部分是因为当时有协调一致的国家政策和沟通，解决了我们目前遇到的一些干扰信息，而且我们有优秀的沟通者。

sentences.en: So the people knew what worked and what didn't.
sentences.zh: 所以人们知道什么有效，什么无效。

sentences.en: They even knew – even gave us good estimates of what this basic reproductive number was.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至知道——甚至能给出基本传染数的良好估算。

sentences.en: That is how transmissible Ebola is.
sentences.zh: 也就是埃博拉的传染性有多强。

sentences.en: So my – I guess I'm an optimist about people's ability to understand these things.
sentences.zh: 所以我——我想我对人们理解这些事物的能力持乐观态度。

sentences.en: You know, people – none of us is perfect, but when the chips are down,
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们——我们谁都不完美，但在关键时刻，

sentences.en: if we're given half a chance through good communications and we have the resources to address – to make and execute good decisions, that people will figure things out.
sentences.zh: 如果我们通过良好的沟通获得了一半的机会，并且有资源来做出和执行正确的决定，人们是能够弄清楚事情的。

sentences.en: So for myself, I've been helping some other people with research projects,
sentences.zh: 所以对我自己来说，我一直在帮助其他人进行研究项目，

sentences.en: but because I've decided not to do any research of my own because I've been working these sort of issues for a long time.
sentences.zh: 但我决定不再亲自做研究，因为我研究这类问题已经很长时间了。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it was more – I've brought greater value by helping to connect to different worlds,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得更有价值的是——我通过帮助连接不同的领域发挥了更大的作用，

sentences.en: like this National Academy of Sciences Committee that I'm going on as the only social or behavioral scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 比如这个美国国家科学院委员会，我是其中唯一的社会或行为科学家。

sentences.en: I figure that's the best thing that I can do.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是我能做的最好的事情。

sentences.en: Are there lessons from your prior research that you would impart to us at this point?
sentences.zh: 你之前的研究中有什么经验教训可以在此时传授给我们吗？

sentences.en: You mentioned your work on Ebola and H5N1.
sentences.zh: 你提到了你对埃博拉和H5N1的研究。

sentences.en: So I think – so I have my lessons for policymaker are to level with the public, treat the public like adults, assume that people can understand well-crafted messages, can execute,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为——我对决策者的建议是坦诚面对公众，把公众当作成年人对待，假设人们能够理解精心制作的信息，能够执行，

sentences.en: can handle bad news, want to know what they're up againSt.
sentences.zh: 能够处理坏消息，并且想要知道他们面对的是什么。

sentences.en: Make certain that you're up against, make certain that you're up against, make certain that you're up against,
sentences.zh: 确保你面对的是什么，确保你面对的是什么，确保你面对的是什么，

sentences.en: make certain that you provide them the resources that they can take care of themselves and their family.
sentences.zh: 确保你为他们提供资源，让他们能够照顾好自己和家人。

sentences.en: There's a tendency upon – on the part of experts, including public officials, to do a lousy job communicating and giving up on the public.
sentences.zh: 专家，包括政府官员，往往倾向于在沟通上做得一团糟，并对公众失去信心。

sentences.en: And typically it's a case where the politicians, the officials have failed the public, not the public has failed the politicians.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，是政客和官员辜负了公众，而不是公众辜负了政客。

sentences.en: My advice for all of us who are trying to make the best out of this situation is to – in terms of practical information, it doesn't change very quickly.
sentences.zh: 对于我们所有试图在这场危机中做到最好的人，我的建议是——就实用信息而言，它不会很快改变。

sentences.en: You could check every morning, check two or three trusted news sources, a local paper if you're still fortunate to have it, a national paper, your local health department.
sentences.zh: 你可以每天早上查看两三个值得信赖的新闻来源，如果还有幸能买到的话，可以看一份当地报纸、一份全国性报纸，以及当地的卫生部门信息。

sentences.en: And that will probably tell you everything that you need to know fact-wise.
sentences.zh: 这大概就能告诉你所有你需要知道的事实。

sentences.en: Use social media for social support, not a source of information.
sentences.zh: 利用社交媒体获取社会支持，而不是将其作为信息来源。

sentences.en: One of the cognitive traps that's very human is to try to make sense out of any claim that we hear.
sentences.zh: 人类的一个认知陷阱就是试图理解我们听到的任何说法。

sentences.en: So you read some fantastic conspiracy theory and you think, well, maybe and who knows.
sentences.zh: 所以你读到一些离奇的阴谋论，你会想，嗯，也许吧，谁知道呢。

sentences.en: And then that natural sense-making function is useful in everyday life when the world isn't trying to lie to you.
sentences.zh: 当世界没有试图欺骗你时，这种自然的理解功能在日常生活中是有用的。

sentences.en: But there's lots of people out there who are trying to lie to you.
sentences.zh: 但外面有很多人试图欺骗你。

sentences.en: So I would say pay no attention to factual claims on the news, on the – on the internet.
sentences.zh: 所以我建议不要理会新闻、互联网上的事实性声明。

sentences.en: And social media or coming from – or coming from politicians.
sentences.zh: 以及社交媒体上或来自政客的声明。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Fischoff, I want to thank you for talking to us yet again.
sentences.zh: 好的，菲施霍夫博士，我想再次感谢你接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting and enlightening.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣且富有启发性。

sentences.en: And I'm sure it's going to help our listeners cope as we deal with the huge changes that we're seeing in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我相信这会帮助我们的听众在我们生活中经历巨大变化时应对挑战。

sentences.en: So thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: And thank you to our listeners.
sentences.zh: 也感谢我们的听众。

sentences.en: If you have any comments or thoughts about our podcast, send us an email at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对我们的播客有任何意见或想法，请发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on Apple, Stitcher, Spotify, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Apple、Stitcher、Spotify 或任何你获取播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》往期节目。

sentences.en: And please consider giving us a rating on those sites.
sentences.zh: 请考虑在这些平台上给我们评分。

sentences.en: You can also go to our website and get all episodes at www.speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 你也可以访问我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 获取所有剧集。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，我是金·米尔斯。
